## 1. How many ratchets?

The catalogue holds **16** ratchets, every one sourced, across all five mechanism types: depth 1, dissipation 7, grade 1, route switch 2, tramp contamination 5. 5 are already inside the model (cu_in_steel, cu_to_other_scrap, cu_in_use_dissipation, cu_ore_grade, cu_depth); the rest are characterised (tolerance, energy step) but not yet coupled into the stock-flow or the cascade. The count is a floor, not a census: each Metal Wheel cell rated *dissolved, harmful* is a candidate tramp ratchet, and there are 13 of them [file params/metal_wheel.yaml].

Energy steps are the energy paid each time one unit goes through the ratchet: for tramp elements and route switches, primary minus secondary production energy of the host; for dissipation, the cradle-to-gate energy of replacing the lost metal from primary (Nuss and Eckelman 2014, Table S38). Ranges come from the parameters' own ranges.


## 2. How do they interact?

Declared interactions (catalogue `interactions`):

| From | Kind | To | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cu_in_steel` | amplifies | `sn_in_steel` | Tin exacerbates hot shortness (Daehn 2017), so the two tolerances are not independent. |
| `cu_in_steel` | fed_by | `cu_to_other_scrap` | Copper collected but not separated travels in steel scrap (Phase 2 link). |
| `sn_in_steel` | amplifies | `cu_in_steel` | Synergistic hot shortness. |
| `alloys_into_carbon_steel` | parallel | `cu_in_steel` | Same thermodynamics (more noble than iron), opposite sign: copper harms the host, nickel is harmless to it but lost. |
| `fe_in_aluminium` | feeds | `al_dilution` | Iron above the wrought limit is diluted with primary aluminium. |
| `si_in_aluminium` | feeds | `al_dilution` | The cast-alloy sink hides the problem only while cast demand grows. |
| `al_dilution` | parallel | `cu_in_steel` | Aluminium's analogue of the copper-in-steel dilution. |
| `zn_to_eaf_dust` | parallel | `cu_in_steel` | Same scrap stream; zinc leaves the melt, copper stays. |
| `cu_to_other_scrap` | feeds | `cu_in_steel` | This flow is the copper load of steel scrap. |
| `cu_to_other_scrap` | feeds | `cu_ore_grade` | Copper lost to steel is replaced from leaner ore. |
| `cu_in_use_dissipation` | feeds | `cu_ore_grade` | Replaced from primary. |
| `cu_ore_grade` | amplifies | `cu_depth` | Leaner ore is also deeper ore in the extraction ordering. |
| `cu_depth` | amplifies | `cu_ore_grade` | See cu_ore_grade. |

The one interaction the model can already measure end to end is copper's: copper that is collected but not separated (`cu_to_other_scrap`) becomes the copper load of steel scrap (`cu_in_steel`), and copper replaced from primary drives `cu_ore_grade` and `cu_depth`. Pulling copper out of that loop with the carbon cup moves all three at once: the steel LP crossover moves from 2121 [run 2b9e9bf0ff80] to 2163 [run afe5881b6c28], the cumulative copper penalty in steel from 7,533 EJ to 5,463 EJ, and the Harmsen bracket's first supply shortfall from 2395 to 2516 [run afe5881b6c28]. A lever on one ratchet acts on its neighbours; levers should be compared on the whole chain.

The Metal Wheel makes the same point from the metallurgy side: whether an element is a ratchet depends on the carrier route it lands in. Nickel is a benign alloying element in steel but lost to the nickel cycle; gold and the PGMs are recovered in the copper route and lost (and harmful) in the steel route; zinc volatilises in the steel route and is the carrier of its own. The routes are the infrastructure, so the ratchet count depends on which infrastructures exist.

**Reading.** Inside the agreed cascade boundary the modelled ratchets move maintenance energy by at most 1.4 % from its 2025 level in the Harmsen bracket [run 2b9e9bf0ff80]: it is 600.0 EJ/yr in 2025 and 594.0 EJ/yr in 2200 [run 2b9e9bf0ff80], with rho(A) near 0.121 [run 2b9e9bf0ff80]. Two things keep the signal small, and neither means the ratchets are small: the energy sector's own use dominates rho(A) (Phase 3 sensitivity), and only copper's ratchets and copper-in-steel are coupled into A(t). The per-unit energy steps in section 1 show where the larger effects sit once coupled: aluminium route switches cost 160.0 MJ per kg diverted [reg rt.al.energy_primary, rt.al.energy_recycling] against 12.6 MJ/kg for steel [reg st.energy.bf_bof, st.energy.scrap_eaf], and dissipated platinum 243,000 MJ/kg [reg rt.ced.pt]. The second clear effect is timing: the ratchets decide *when* the copper and steel constraints bind (crossover and shortfall years above), which a fixed-final-demand cascade shows as a change of date more than of level.


## 5. Design lever: the carbon cup

Carbon-reducible metals housed in burnable, separable carbon sub-matrices; at end of life the product is burnt, the metal reports to the ash as oxide and carbon reduces it. Eligibility is Ellingham-based: carbon must reduce the metal's most stable oxide at or below cc.t_max = 1773 K [reg cc.t_max].

Every carbon-cup parameter is an explicit assumption with a wide range [reg cc.biogenic_share, cc.capture_fraction, cc.carbon_per_metal, cc.collection, cc.matrix_net_energy, cc.processing, cc.t_max]. The direction of the result is robust in this model: better copper separation lowers maintenance energy and delays both copper and steel constraints. Its size is set mostly by the cup share and cup processing rate; the CO2 stream scales with carbon per kg of metal; and the net matrix energy, set to zero by default, can reverse the energy result if the matrix costs much more energy to make than burning it returns.


## 6. Open items

Parameters still resting on assumptions (21): `cas.al.alumina_per_al`, `cas.al.smelting_electricity`, `cas.ammonia_per_explosive`, `cas.ce.limestone_per_clinker`, `cas.cu.secondary_energy`, `cas.cu_energy_net_of_inputs`, `cas.en.coal_per_mj`, `cas.st.rock_per_ore`, `cc.biogenic_share`, `cc.capture_fraction`, `cc.carbon_per_metal`, `cc.collection`, `cc.matrix_net_energy`, `cc.processing`, `cc.t_max`, `dem.growth_calibration_years`, `dem.population_hold_year`, `geo.discovery_smoothing_years`, `geo.max_discovery_rate`, `st.allocation_pinch`, `st.cu_to_process_losses`.

Not yet coupled into the model: the aluminium, glass, polymer and specialty-metal ratchets (characterised only); the Metal Wheel's `unknown` cells (mostly the Ni/Cr and Sn routes, which no radar sector covers); energy-sector quality (falling EROI) as a ratchet of its own.
